title: Packs on the map
description: The pack model as the map's own words: a pack is an item, and everything it declares is an item part_of it (a type, a link type, a rule, a view, a screen, an instruction, a style, a lens, a layout, a part, an automation), each recording the shipped value it last came from (shipped) and naming the code it runs by path and hash (runs). The types are core's, since the kernel reads them; this pack keeps the ties between them: what a part requires, what a type is a flavour of, and what an owner's version stands over. packs/pack_model/README.md is the contract the registry, install and floor build on.

links.title: requires
links.description: A pack, or a part of one, cannot work without what the target provides: the name it requires is the link's props.name (type:task, has:when, field:due@task, service:answer.flat), the target the part that provides it now. Made by install from the pack file's requires and what each part names; a name nothing on the map provides has no link, and its pack waits.

links.title: flavour of
links.description: A type is a flavour of its parent, a link type of the one it extends: drawn from spec.extends, which stays the truth the registry reads. Made by install beside the spec.

links.title: stands over
links.description: The owner's version of a shipped part stands over it: the source's fields are read over the target's, and an upgrade changes the target alone. Drawn from the source's preset, which names the target's declares; one part has one version at most. A rule's version may only tighten the floor's.
